answer_raw:
The fastest option is a **GPU Droplet** using DigitalOcean's 1-Click Models for zero-config deployment [3], while the cheapest way to run a 7B model is via **Serverless Inference** [1].

For the fastest performance, you would rent a **GPU Droplet** which allows you to deploy models like Llama variants or DeepSeek R1 directly through a partnership with Hugging Face [3]. While the specific monthly price for a GPU Droplet is not listed in the provided documentation, you can expect to pay for dedicated GPU resources or use the **1-Click Models** menu to deploy small open models [1].

Regarding the cheapest way to run a 7B model, **Serverless Inference** is the most cost-effective path because it is billed by usage and provides an OpenAI-compatible API without the need to manage a full server [1][4]. For a 7B-class model (like Qwen 2.5 7B), you can use these serverless endpoints to pay only for the inference you actually perform [1]. 

If you require a dedicated virtual machine (Droplet) rather than serverless, the cheapest hardware to run a 7B model locally would typically involve a machine with enough RAM/VRAM to handle a quantized version of the model; for example, a used base M1 with 16GB can run 7B-class models (~$300s-undated) [6]. However, DigitalOcean's own pricing for base Droplets starts at **$5/mo** (undated) but does not specify the minimum specs required to run a 7 stuck-on-disk 7B model; you would need to check their current Droplet spec requirements to see if their lowest-tier CPU/RAM combinations can handle the inference load [2].
